title: What’s your favorite core game loop for an open-world multiplayer RPG?
author: SneakerHunterDev
selftext:
Hey everyone!  
I’m developing a 2D casual online RPG with a large open world, lots of character & world customization, weapon crafting, and other sandbox-style features. All the features are AI based and live generated in the game. If you want to take a look at the game, here is the [steam page](https://theflairgame.com?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=coregameplayloop&utm_term=aigamedev).

Right now, players can already do a lot - but after some time, they start to feel like they’re running out of clear goals or structure. To fix that, I’m planning to add optional game modes to keep things engaging and create more player interaction.

Think of something like GTA Online, but in a top-down 2D world.

So here’s my question:  
What’s your favorite type of core game loop or mode in an open-world multiplayer setting?

Some ideas I’ve been exploring:

* A battle royale-style event
* Random “zones” appearing in the world where players fight off NPC waves (solo or co-op)
* Something completely different that encourages cooperation or competition

I’d love to hear what kind of core loops you find the most fun or rewarding in these kinds of games!

comments.author: bob101910
comments.body:
I like having a base, city, or house to upgrade. Go out, get resources from battle, then build at a safe place. Think Ball X Pit as a recent example. 


Looking at the Steam page, if there is no limit to what the player can create, anything else in the game is pointless. 

Why do world events if I can just create the reward? Some if somebody creates a nuke and destroys everything I own? Guy near me keeps creating hyper realistic penis pictures and I don't want to see it, why would I want to keep playing?

replies.author: SneakerHunterDev
replies.body: Yeah okay, maybe ”No limits“ is a Little too much. You Can Create all the Assets like characters, weapons, buildings by yourself
